responses:
The only tender document in the repo is `tenders/T-2026-014/tender.md`. If that's the RFQ you mean, **this extraction fails the check.** IP66 meets the requirement, but the source citation is wrong and the applicability is incomplete.

| Field | Extraction says | Tender actually says | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source | RFQ p.3, section 2.1 | Clause **4.5**, Section 4 (Electrical requirements), `tenders/T-2026-014/tender.md:25`. The document has no page numbers and no section 2. | ❌ Wrong reference |
| Quoted text | "Enclosures shall be IP65 or better." | "**Panel and motor terminal enclosures** shall be IP65 or better." | ❌ Quote is not exact; the subject was dropped |
| Applicability | All panels | Panels **and motor terminal enclosures**. That means the P-01 (90 kW) and P-02 (37 kW) motor terminal boxes too. | ❌ Incomplete |
| Requirement | IP65 | IP65 minimum ("or better") | ✅ |
| Our offer | IP66 | Under IEC 60529, codes up to 6 are cumulative. IP66 has the same dust rating as IP65 (6) and survives stronger water jets (6 vs 5), so IP66 counts as "better." | ✅ Meets it, for the panels |

**What to fix**
1. Change the source to clause 4.5 and quote it word for word.
2. Change applicability to "panels and motor terminal enclosures (P-01, P-02)."
3. Confirm the IP rating of the motor terminal boxes. Nothing in the extraction shows that IP66 (or at least IP65) covers them. P-01's terminal box also has to work with the Ex d certification required by 4.3, because the wet well is Zone 1 (Annex B).

**Related points to check (not part of this requirement)**
- Clause 9.2 sets a 50 °C ambient design temperature. Make sure the IP66 panels are rated for that, especially sealed enclosures that need cooling.
- Section 9 overrides Sections 4 and 7 (clause 9.3). Nothing in Section 9 changes the IP rating, so 4.5 still stands.

**What I couldn't verify**
- The repo has no extraction or analysis file and no offer document, so I couldn't confirm that the offer really says IP66. I checked only the text you pasted.
- The "p.3 section 2.1" reference might come from a different RFQ (for example, a PDF that isn't in the repo). If so, send it to me and I'll check against that instead.

A wrong clause number that still has the right value usually means the extractor paraphrased instead of quoting. Spot-check the other extracted requirements from this tender for the same problem.
